clue.text: Oz's wet blanket makes an impression on American casualty!

parts.note: to make an impression on people is to wow them
ER, the emergency room, is the American name for a hospital casualty department

explanation.surface: An exclamation about an Australian spoilsport shaping up as a US hospital patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link. ER is the US term for what Britain calls Casualty, the hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a puritanical killjoy or spoilsport is called a wowser.

clue.text: See 2
Mad idea from a bewildered widow; could be available to all for three short weeks!

definitions.text: could be available to all for three short weeks

indicators.note: mad says the letters of the phrase that follows are jumbled, with the word idea among them

parts.note: the sixteen letters of this phrase supply the answer together with those of idea
the letters of this word are taken out of the jumble, leaving the answer

explanation.surface: A grieving widow has a crazy notion about something open to everyone for a brief spell.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus IDEA rearranges into A BEWILDERED WIDOW. The definition plays on WWW, three Ws, W being the short form of week.
explanation.definitionFit: The internet's hypertext system is open to everyone, and its usual address prefix is three letter Ws, each the abbreviation of week.

clue.text: Steganographer will call for pint measure first

indicators.note: first says the measure is placed at the front, before the other two pieces

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
to cry is to call out

explanation.surface: Someone who hides messages asks for a pint glass before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. The definition is the verb phrase: what a steganographer, a hider of secret messages, will do.
explanation.definitionFit: A steganographer conceals messages, so what such a person will do is put them into secret code.

clue.text: Counterfeit coin?

explanation.surface: A forged piece of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To counterfeit can mean to fabricate or make up, and to coin a word is to devise something new.

clue.text: Engraving that is with lines in the negative

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation and the lines inside the negative word

parts.note: no is the negative reply
ie, id est, is the abbreviation for that is
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: An engraving with lines that appears as a photographic negative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two pieces placed inside NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Niello is a black metallic inlay used to fill engraved designs on silver, and the word also names such decorative engraved work.

clue.text: Shakespearian singers at the Coliseum bristle at the Guardian

parts.note: ENO, English National Opera, performs at the London Coliseum
a barb is a bristle-like hooked hair or point
the newspaper's own voice is we, so us

explanation.surface: Opera singers at a London theatre take offence at a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link. The London Coliseum is the home theatre of English National Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Enobarbus is a character in Antony and Cleopatra, Antony's friend who deserts him.

clue.text: Sound sense in church, if replacing sad characters during the day

indicators.note: replacing says the word if takes the place of the jumbled letters of sad

parts.note: Thursday is a day of the week
the characters, or letters, of sad, here in a different order
taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchgoer senses something on a day when a gloomy mood gives way to doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is a link. The definition: to cense, which sounds like sense, is to perfume with incense in church.
explanation.definitionFit: To thurify is to burn incense before something, which is to cense it, a homophone of sense.

clue.text: He 4-ed the 2 1down, investing Swiss capital in steel rim production

indicators.note: investing means wrapping around, so the anagram encloses the capital
production says the letters of steel rim are worked into a new form

parts.note: Berne is the capital of Switzerland

explanation.surface: A tale of a famous inventor, with Swiss money put into making steel wheel rims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. BERNE goes inside an anagram of STEEL RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The British computer scientist devised the internet's hypertext system at CERN in 1989.

clue.text: Recreate over the river

indicators.note: over says the word for recreate is turned round

parts.note: to recreate something is to redo it

explanation.surface: An instruction to make something again over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a central European river forming much of the border between Germany and Poland.

clue.text: Entreaty impossible from Le Tin Man?

definitions.text: Entreaty impossible from Le Tin Man?

parts.words: Entreaty impossible from Le Tin Man?
parts.note: the Tin Man of Oz has no heart, so a French cry from the heart is beyond him

explanation.surface: A plea the heartless Wizard of Oz character, given a French article, could never make.
explanation.walkthrough: The French 'Le' hints the answer is a French phrase meaning a cry from the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A passionate appeal or protest is called, in a French phrase, a cry from the heart.

clue.text: Was dubious theologian the Unknown Soldier?

indicators.note: dubious says the letters of was are put in doubtful order

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Asking whether a questionable religious scholar was the soldier in the famous tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unknown Soldier' reads as a phrase, but the Unknown is Y and Soldier alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaddy is old British slang for a private soldier.

clue.text: Sour grapes from Modena when black Islamic avenger goes East for a conversion

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: conversion says the combined letters are changed into a new order
goes, with for, says the letter for East leaves and the letter a takes its place

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tale of a religious avenger travelling east and changing his faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' and 'for' are links. Black goes first; the Modena grapes hint at the Italian condiment, and the Islamic avenger is pure surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsamic vinegar is made from grape must in Modena, and vinegar is literally soured wine.

clue.text: Tergiversation going for a Burton? But that's not British!

indicators.note: going for a Burton is British slang for being wrecked, so the letters that follow are wrecked

parts.note: these letters are jumbled

indicators.note: not says the British letter is removed from but

explanation.surface: Changing sides likened to being killed off, with a protest that the phrase is not British.
explanation.walkthrough: To go for a Burton is RAF slang for to be killed or ruined. BUT less B gives UT, which joins A BURTON in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Tergiversation means a change of allegiance or opinion, a complete reversal of position.

clue.text: No corruption with this beneath the signet

definitions.text: No corruption with this beneath the signet

parts.words: No corruption with this beneath the signet
parts.note: a coating protecting a car underside from rust, read as something placed beneath a seal ring

explanation.surface: An official document kept honest by being placed under a seal ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Corruption hints at corrosion; the phrase split in two means beneath the seal.
explanation.definitionFit: Underseal is a protective coating applied to a vehicle's underside to stop rusting.

clue.text: Do as you're told, you old b---, and ring back!

indicators.note: back says the whole string of pieces is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
the letter b, standing for the censored word
o is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An exasperated order to a disobedient person, with a mild expletive, to phone back.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes after b hide a rude word; only the B counts. YE B O turned round gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply with an instruction or command is exactly doing what you are told.

clue.text: Have daily involvement with the scriptures

indicators.note: involvement says the answer is wrapped up inside the words have daily

explanation.surface: Advice to make daily study of holy texts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vedas are the oldest sacred scriptures of Hinduism.

clue.text: See 12
In truth, American tramps are given to circumlocution

indicators.note: in places the tramps inside the word for truth

parts.note: verity means truth
a bo, short for hobo, is an American tramp

explanation.surface: An admission that US vagrants tend to talk round the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are given to' is a link. 'In truth' reads as 'honestly', but it is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbosity is wordiness, the use of more words than needed, like roundabout speech.

clue.text: A touching sight?

parts.note: a moving scene, read as a way of seeing by touch for the blind

explanation.surface: Something emotionally moving to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised-dot writing system lets blind people read by touch, a kind of sight through fingertips.

clue.text: Strength or depth in the Scriptures

parts.note: thew means muscle or strength

explanation.surface: Asking whether the Bible holds power or profundity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Word, as in the Word of God, is a name for the Bible or scripture.

clue.text: Soundly chased before losing it, was she?

definitions.text: Soundly chased before losing it, was she?

parts.words: Soundly chased before losing it, was she?
parts.note: chased said aloud is chaste, and a woman chaste until she lost something lost this quality

explanation.surface: A woman pursued hard before she lost her nerve, or her way.
explanation.walkthrough: Chased is said like chaste, the quality a woman was thought to lose with her chastity.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastity was traditionally called a woman's virtue, the thing she was said to lose.

clue.text: Art lines badly drawn from William Wallace, were they?

definitions.text: drawn from William Wallace, were they?

indicators.note: badly says the letters of art lines are put into a poor, distorted order

explanation.surface: Poor lines in a portrait of the Scottish hero.
explanation.walkthrough: William Wallace, the Scottish patriot, was hanged, drawn and quartered in 1305; being drawn meant disembowelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Being drawn as a punishment meant having the bowels removed, so these innards were drawn from him.

clue.text: Briefly, the biographer to the Franco-British-Spanish king

parts.note: au is French for to the
rey is Spanish for king

explanation.surface: A short note on a writer serving a monarch of three nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Franco' marks AU as French. John Aubrey wrote the short biographies 'Brief Lives', hence 'Briefly'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Aubrey was the seventeenth-century antiquary famous for his biographical sketches, Brief Lives.

clue.text: With America supporting opening of Battle of Hastings

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit below the first letter
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: and means with or plus

explanation.surface: An account of the start of a famous 1066 battle, with American help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. Hastings is not the battle but Hastings Banda, first president of Malawi.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings Banda led Malawi from independence, so his first name defines his surname.

clue.text: Brewing fifty Grade A tea bags

indicators.note: brewing stirs up the letters, as tea is brewed

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Making a pot using fifty top-quality tea bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea bags' reads as one thing, but bags alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags is informal for lots, as in bags of time, meaning a large amount.

clue.text: High time Will Kane faced Frank Miller

definitions.text: High time Will Kane faced Frank Miller

parts.words: High time Will Kane faced Frank Miller
parts.note: in the western High ..., Marshal Will Kane faces the outlaw Frank Miller at midday

explanation.surface: A summary of the climax of a classic Western film.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is when the sun is highest, and the High Noon showdown takes place then.

clue.text: Poor assistance for cartographers?

definitions.meaning: historic aid given to the poor by parishes
map-makers show raised land shapes on special maps

explanation.surface: Inadequate help offered to map-makers.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor relief was aid for the needy; a relief map shows terrain heights, used by mapmakers.

clue.text: Recognition proverbially inherent in 20

definitions.meaning: something given in acknowledgement of merit
the proverb says goodness carries its own prize

explanation.surface: Acknowledgement that, so the saying goes, comes built into a moral quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'virtue is its own reward'; 20 refers to that entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize or recompense given for merit is a form of recognition.
